design.affected_system: multimodal evacuation, assisted transport, and emergency access network
alternatives: protect minimum coverage before needs-based allocation of assisted evacuation vehicles and support teams
adapt allocations using observed demand, uptake, and capacity for assisted evacuation vehicles and support teams
pair priority- and time-window-constrained fleet allocation with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Evacuation demand, assistance eligibility, vehicle capacity, route state, and hazard timing are versioned.
Compliance, household departure, and network degradation remain observed inputs or bounded scenarios.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
design.baseline: retain the current distribution rule for assisted evacuation vehicles and support teams.

constraints.description: The evacuation and emergency mobility allocate must respect declared minimum service, eligibility, capacity, and distributional safeguards.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

design.decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
design.decision_owner: emergency transportation coordinator and incident commander
design.decision_question: How should accessible vehicles, drivers, escorts, and medical transport slots be assigned?

independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for assisted evacuation vehicles and support teams passes documented checks for eligible denominators, group attributes, inventory, minimum-service rules, and allocation records.

design.intended_claim: A versioned allocate design for comparing declared alternatives affecting assisted evacuation vehicles and support teams, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: eligible evacuation needs without assigned transport
distributional gap in eligible evacuation needs without assigned transport
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not report assigned transport as passenger contact, pickup, or safe arrival.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for assisted evacuation vehicles and support teams passes documented checks for eligible denominators, group attributes, inventory, minimum-service rules, and allocation records.

design.title: Allocate accessible vehicles and emergency mobility teams
transportability_risks: Hazards, vehicle ownership, disability access, road topology, trust, and compliance differ.
